text: "At 1700 we took picket station #1, 12 miles bearing 060°T from our group."
Walker, Weeks and Haynsworth assigned picket stations; "enemy plans to attack in force tomorrow" (as quoted by Irons; not yet checked on the scan).
source: Irons, Phalanx Against the Divine Wind, quoting Waldron's war diary

text: Task Force point option 26-50N 129-10E. Pickets for the day: Haynsworth #1 (060°); Weeks #2X (000°); Walker #12 (300°).
Two Saiun and an Army Type 100 scout leave to find the carriers. They report two groups (six carriers) south of Amami-Ōshima.
source: Fifth Air Fleet operations record, pp. 11-13

text: A Saiun reports 4 carriers at 「メツ三ス」, the 20-minute square 27-00N to 27-20N, 129-40E to 130-00E. Haynsworth's 0800 fix is 10-20 nm west of it.
source: Recon 11 message log and results table, pp. 23-29, 37-38

text: "爆戦三〇機 彗星二三機 一〇一五—一三一〇間逐次発進": 30 bomb-carrying Zeros and 23 Suisei take off one after another between 1015 and 1310 to attack the carrier force southeast of Amami-Ōshima.
source: Fifth Air Fleet operations record, pp. 11-13

text: Suisei unit, first attack: 11 Suisei from First Kokubu to search for and attack the carrier force (including 4 carriers) southeast of Amami-Ōshima, at 「メツミス」. Led by Lt. 野村浩三.
source: 210th Air Group action report, narrative, form p. 9

text: Dinah splashed by the task group's CAP at 330°-29 mi.
Four Suisei turn back (野村/矢島; 宮尾/佐守; 鈴木/新谷; 新屋/長嶺). The time reads 1015 or 1115.
source: 210th Air Group action report, form p. 9; crew list form p. 23

text: "Two JUDYs shot down by ESSEX CAP at 035-35": on Haynsworth's side of the group, 70 minutes before she was hit.
Zeke splashed at 350-16.
The 210th's fighter escort, over Amami at 1140, fights Hellcats about 80 nm south of Tokunoshima.
"One JUDY shot down by ESSEX CAP at 000-20".
Fix 26-55N 129-31E. South Dakota at 26-41-45N 129-25-30E.
source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 3; South Dakota war diary

text: Seven Zekes intercepted at 000-15; one to five splashed. Cabot: a large group intercepted 40 mi north, "CAP broke up the raid".
source: Essex chronology, p. 34; Cabot war diary, p. 12

text: Two large groups of unidentified planes closing.

A Judy "sneaking into the disposition under the cover of the interception" comes in on Cabot from astern, drops its bomb about 100 yd off her starboard quarter, loses a wing to gunfire and falls off her bow. Astoria calls it "tentatively ... a Zeke".
source: Cabot war diary, p. 12; North Carolina p. 5; Astoria pp. 64-66

text: Recovering CAP #2: 1st Lt. J. H. Carpenter missing, "last seen diving on an enemy aircraft during a dog fight following an interception".
"全機敵KdBニ突入セルモノト推定": all seven aircraft presumed to have dived into the enemy carrier force, 1230 to 1300. Results unknown. Planned bombing altitude 400 m.
source: 210th Air Group action report, form pp. 9 and 17

text: "1232 C/C to 020°T ... The SC-3 radar picked up bogey at 010°, distance 22 miles ... Fighters vectored out from task group merged with bogey on scope until raid had passed close aboard port beam."
"The sound of dog-fight and machine gun fire" is heard and tracked from the port bow to the beam. "A Judy or Zeke" is splashed 1,500 yards on the port quarter.

A Judy "appeared out of the clouds in a very steep dive" with a Corsair on each side. All three "pulled up sharply short of the water"; the Corsairs climbed into the cloud, and the Judy flattened out and "headed away from the ship". Speed increased to 25 knots.
source: Action report, p. 3; war diary p. 3

text: Fire opened at 1,500 yards, altitude 150 ft: 20 mm, 40 mm and 5-inch. The Judy turns to starboard, "wing over" and comes back at the ship. Its bomb, "released or ... knocked off in the turn", falls about 1,000 yards abeam.

"With wings at 45° angle, striking at 1250 Item" in the main radio transmitter room, abaft the bridge, at the twin 40 mm mount 41. A gasoline fireball goes through Main Radio, the 40 mm platform, CIC and plot.
Seven men are killed outright, five of them in or beside mount 41's crew (Report of Casualties, items 1-7).
source: Report of Casualties, action report p. 22; Irons for mount 41's crew

text: "Seven dead, eleven critically wounded, fourteen slightly wounded." Fires under control in about ten minutes ("By 13??", overstruck), out in about fifty-five. Radio and radar out: she rejoins the group and is coached on station by other ships.
source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 4; action report pp. 3-5

text: "Out of a 15 plane enemy raid, 2 ZEKE's closed": a suicide Zeke in a shallow dive clips Cabot's SK radar antenna and explodes close aboard. Bunker Hill calls it "another JUDY". At 1302 Washington shoots down a suicide Zeke attacking Hancock.
source: Cabot p. 12; Astoria p. 72; Bunker Hill diary p. 8; VBF-6 history pp. 21-22

text: A friendly 5-inch shell hits North Carolina's No. 2 director: 3 killed, 44 wounded.
"At 1318 HAYNSWORTH was hit by suicide plane at number 41 twin 40 MM mount. All radar and radio out, 7 KIA, 14 WIA." After the hit Waldron takes station #1.
"At 1321 the U.S.S. HAYNSWORTH reported having received a bomb hit." Her radio was wrecked, so the report came late or by another ship.
22 enemy planes reported destroyed by CAP and gunfire. TG 58.3's report: a persistent 2-hour attack beginning at 1055; CAP shot down 19 and AA 3.
source: South Dakota war diary; TG 58.3 report p. 38

text: Second attack: two Suisei (Lt. 鈴木文夫) find nothing. The No. 2 plane's track chart survives: off Kokubu at 1410, farthest south at 1535 under rain cloud (cloud 10, base 500-900 m), north past Amami, Nakanoshima and Kuchinoerabu, landing at Tanegashima at 1750.
source: 210th track chart (別図第四), C13120082800 p. 12

text: Four Suisei of 第三御盾隊 take off against the carriers 85 nm east of northern Okinawa; one claims a battleship's stern at about 1835. Too late to be Haynsworth's attacker.
Eleven of the wounded are transferred to South Dakota on 6 April, three more on the 7th. By 9 April "five additional deaths" aboard her bring "the total to twelve (12)".
The dead are buried at sea, weighted with live 5-inch rounds (Irons, from crew diaries or letters; not in the war diary or action report).
source: Irons, Phalanx Against the Divine Wind

text: Detached from TG 58.3 with Hancock and Cabot for Ulithi; Pearl Harbor 27 April; Mare Island repairs from 3 May.
source: Haynsworth war diary, p. 4; South Dakota war diary
